question: Which international city hosted the historic conference that formally launched Primary Health Care in 1978?
explanation: The Declaration of Alma-Ata was adopted at the international conference held in Kazakhstan in 1978, setting the foundation for global primary health initiatives. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h1)

question: What was the main shift in healthcare delivery brought about by the 1978 Alma-Ata Declaration?

options.A: Focusing exclusively on urban populations with high disease burdens
options.B: Moving from centralized hospital-based curative care to community-focused preventive health
options.C: Eliminating all specialized medical care in favor of traditional herbal remedies
options.D: Transferring the funding of all global health systems to the private sector

explanation: Alma-Ata challenged the old model of expensive, city-centered hospitals and prioritized accessible, preventive, and community-based services. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h1)

question: What is the underlying ethical philosophy upon which Primary Health Care is built?
explanation: Primary Health Care treats health as a basic human right, anchoring its entire delivery model on principles of fairness and social justice. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h2)

question: Why is Primary Health Care considered more than just a lower level of clinical services?

options.A: It operates exclusively within private hospital networks without government oversight
options.B: It rejects modern scientific medicine in favor of localized practices
options.C: It only deals with emergency room referrals and major surgical procedures
options.D: It encompasses an entire philosophy of health system organization and community empowerment

explanation: Primary Health Care represents a comprehensive approach to organizing society for health, integrating prevention, treatment, and community development. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h2)

question: What does equitable distribution of health services primarily seek to address?

options.A: The equal distribution of advanced surgical equipment to every clinic
options.B: The standardization of hospital building designs across different countries
options.C: Disparities in access between urban and rural or rich and poor populations
options.D: The elimination of all private healthcare practices globally

explanation: Equitable distribution focuses on bridging the gap so marginalized and rural groups have the same access to care as privileged populations. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h3)

question: A local government health department shifts funding from a large city teaching hospital to build and staff rural health posts. Which core principle does this action best demonstrate?
explanation: Reallocating resources to underserved areas to close the access gap is a textbook application of equitable distribution. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h3)

question: What is the primary role of the community in true Primary Health Care models?

options.A: Passive recipients who simply follow instructions given by visiting doctors
options.B: Active participants in planning, implementing, and evaluating health programs
options.C: Strictly regulatory bodies that penalize healthcare workers for errors
options.D: Financial donors who fund the construction of large referral hospitals

explanation: Empowerment relies on the community driving their own health initiatives rather than just receiving aid passively. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h4)

question: Why is community participation essential for the long-term success of health interventions?

options.A: It prevents community members from ever falling ill with chronic diseases
options.B: It ensures that foreign organizations maintain total control over project budgets
options.C: It allows the government to completely withdraw all funding from the health sector
options.D: It builds local ownership and ensures programs match cultural values and real needs

explanation: When communities design and own their health programs, the interventions fit local realities and continue to function sustainably. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h4)

question: Which of the following sectors outside of medicine directly impacts community health outcomes?

options.D: Stock market trading and corporate finance

explanation: Food production, clean water projects, and literacy are foundational social determinants managed by non-health sectors. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h5)

question: Why must health workers engage with other government sectors when addressing community health?

options.A: Intersectoral meetings are legally required before writing any nursing care plan
options.B: Hospital budgets are exclusively managed by the ministry of agriculture
options.C: Doctors and nurses do not have enough training to diagnose common infectious diseases
options.D: The root causes of illness, such as poor sanitation and malnutrition, lie outside the health sector

explanation: Disease prevention requires tackling social determinants like clean water and food security, which demand cross-ministerial cooperation. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h5)

question: What defines appropriate technology in the context of Primary Health Care?

options.A: Complex equipment that requires specialized foreign technicians to repair
options.B: Scientific soundness, affordability, and adaptability to local resources
options.C: The most expensive and advanced diagnostic machinery available globally
options.D: Exclusive reliance on ancient traditional practices without scientific backing

explanation: Appropriate technology balances scientific validity with economic feasibility and local usability. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which scenario best illustrates the principle of appropriate technology in a rural health clinic?

options.A: Using solar-powered refrigerators to maintain vaccine potency in an area with erratic grid electricity
options.B: Installing an imported computerized tomography scanner that requires a dedicated air-conditioned room
options.C: Purchasing expensive branded intravenous drugs when generic oral alternatives are readily available
options.D: Relying entirely on verbal symptom reporting without using any physical assessment tools

explanation: Solar refrigeration solves a local infrastructure challenge practically and sustainably, fitting the definition of appropriate technology. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h6)

question: Which of the following is formally recognized as one of the essential components of Primary Health Care?
explanation: Immunization is a core pillar of the essential services outlined in the foundational declarations of Primary Health Care. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h7)

question: What is the primary rationale for including safe water and basic sanitation among the core components of Primary Health Care?

options.A: It ensures that local hospitals have enough water pressure to run laundry services
options.B: Sanitation programs are only necessary for urban populations living in high-rise buildings
options.C: Clean water supply is solely the responsibility of private bottled water corporations
options.D: Environmental hygiene prevents the transmission of waterborne and infectious diseases at the source

explanation: Safe water and sanitation tackle environmental determinants, stopping diseases like cholera and typhoid before clinical treatment is needed. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h7)

question: At which level of government are primary health care facilities primarily administered in Nigeria?
explanation: In Nigeria's health system structure, primary health care is decentralized and managed at the Local Government Area level. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h8)

question: A community health nurse in a rural Nigerian village notices low turnout for routine childhood immunizations. What is the most appropriate first step in line with PHC principles?

options.A: Wait passively in the clinic until mothers decide to bring their children on their own
options.B: Engage community elders and local leaders to discuss barriers and plan culturally appropriate outreach
options.C: Report the entire village to federal law enforcement authorities for neglecting child health
options.D: Close the primary health center permanently and relocate all nursing staff to an urban hospital

explanation: Community participation and empowerment require partnering with local leaders to understand and resolve health barriers collaboratively. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h8)
